Data Structures
Part 4: Data Classes
Similar to dictionaries, but
trading flexibility for consistency
and better code completion.

Data Classes
A data class is a class designed primarily to store a related collection of
data.
Unlike dictionaries, data classes define exactly which fields an object is
expected to have, reducing mistakes caused by misspelled or
inconsistent dictionary keys.
Type annotations can also describe what type of data should be stored in
each field, making the structure easier to understand and allowing
development tools to identify some mistakes.
Data classes are especially useful when your program repeatedly works
with the same type of structured data.
